Model Creation

insurance_data$sex_male   <- as.integer(insurance_data$sex   == "male")
insurance_data$smoker_yes <- as.integer(insurance_data$smoker == "yes")
insurance_data$region_id <- as.integer(factor(insurance_data$region,
                                              levels = c("northeast","northwest","southeast","southwest")))

N <- nrow(insurance_data)
y <- insurance_data$charges

Model 1: Intercept-Only

Data model
\[ y_i \sim \operatorname{LogNormal}(\mu,\;\sigma^2) \quad i = 1,\dots,N \]

Priors
\[ \mu \;\sim\; \mathcal{N}(0,\;100^2), \qquad \sigma^2 \;\sim\; \operatorname{InvGamma}(0.01,\,0.01) \]

model1_code = "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  vector<lower=0>[N] y;
}
parameters {
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> sigmasq;
}
transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma = sqrt(sigmasq);
}
model {
  mu       ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  sigmasq  ~ inv_gamma(.01, .01);
  y        ~ lognormal(mu, sigma);
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] yrep;
  real log_lik[N];
  for (j in 1:N) {
    yrep[j]    = lognormal_rng(mu, sigma);
    log_lik[j] = lognormal_lpdf(y[j] | mu, sigma);
  }
}
"
model1_data = list(N = N, y = y)

if (!file.exists("model1_mod.rda")) {
  model1_mod <- stan_model(model_code = model1_code)
  save(model1_mod, file = "model1_mod.rda", compress = "xz")
} else {
  load("model1_mod.rda")
}

fit1 <- sampling(model1_mod,
                 data = model1_data,
                 iter=10000, warmup=5000, seed = 101, chains = 4, refresh = 0)

Convergence check

stan_dens(fit1,
          pars = c("mu", "sigmasq"),
          separate_chains = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Model 1: Posterior Densities for μ and σ²")

Model 2: + Age & BMI

Linear predictor
\[ \eta_i = \beta_0 + \beta_{\text{age}}\,\text{age}_i + \beta_{\text{bmi}}\,\text{bmi}_i \]

Data model
\[ y_i \sim \operatorname{LogNormal}(\eta_i,\;\sigma^2) \]

Priors
\[ \beta_0,\;\beta_{\text{age}},\;\beta_{\text{bmi}} \;\sim\; \mathcal{N}(0,\;100^2), \quad \sigma^2 \;\sim\; \operatorname{InvGamma}(0.01,\,0.01) \]

model2_code = "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  vector<lower=0>[N] y;
  vector[N] age;
  vector[N] bmi;
}
parameters {
  real beta0;
  real beta_age;
  real beta_bmi;
  real<lower=0> sigmasq;
}
transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma = sqrt(sigmasq);
}
model {
  beta0    ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_age ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_bmi ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  sigmasq  ~ inv_gamma(.01, .01);
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n = beta0 + beta_age * age[n] + beta_bmi * bmi[n];
    y[n]     ~ lognormal(mu_n, sigma);
  }
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] yrep;
  real log_lik[N];
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n    = beta0 + beta_age * age[n] + beta_bmi * bmi[n];
    yrep[n]      = lognormal_rng(mu_n, sigma);
    log_lik[n]   = lognormal_lpdf(y[n] | mu_n, sigma);
  }
}
"
model2_data = list(
  N   = N,
  y   = y,
  age = insurance_data$age,
  bmi = insurance_data$bmi
)

if (!file.exists("model2_mod.rda")) {
  model2_mod <- stan_model(model_code = model2_code)
  save(model2_mod, file = "model2_mod.rda", compress = "xz")
} else {
  load("model2_mod.rda")
}

fit2 <- sampling(model2_mod,
                 data = model2_data,
                iter=10000, warmup=5000, seed = 101, chains = 4, refresh = 0)

Convergence check

stan_dens(fit2,
          pars = c("beta0", "beta_age", "beta_bmi", "sigmasq"),
          separate_chains = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Model 2: Posterior Densities for β₀, βₐ₉ₑ, β_{bmi}, σ²")

Model 3: + Children, Sex, Smoker, Region

Linear predictor
\[ \begin{aligned} \eta_i = \beta_0 &+ \beta_{\text{age}}\,\text{age}_i + \beta_{\text{bmi}}\,\text{bmi}_i + \beta_{\text{children}}\,\text{children}_i \\ &+ \beta_{\text{sex}}\,\text{sex}_i + \beta_{\text{smoker}}\,\text{smoker}_i + \beta_{\text{SE}}\,\text{region_SE}_i + \beta_{\text{SW}}\,\text{region_SW}_i + \beta_{\text{NW}}\,\text{region_NW}_i \end{aligned} \]

Data model
\[ y_i \sim \operatorname{LogNormal}(\eta_i,\;\sigma^2) \]

Priors
\[ \beta_j \;\sim\; \mathcal{N}(0,\;100^2) \quad\forall j,\qquad \sigma^2 \;\sim\; \operatorname{InvGamma}(0.01,\,0.01) \]

model3_code = "
data {
  int<lower=1>       N;
  vector<lower=0>[N] y;
  vector[N]          age;
  vector[N]          bmi;
  int<lower=0>       children[N];   
  vector[N]          sex;
  vector[N]          smoker;
  vector[N]          region_SE;
  vector[N]          region_SW;
  vector[N]          region_NW;
}
parameters {
  real              beta0;
  real              beta_age;
  real              beta_bmi;
  real              beta_children;
  real              beta_sex;
  real              beta_smoker;
  real              beta_se;
  real              beta_sw;
  real              beta_nw;
  real<lower=0>      sigmasq;
}
transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma = sqrt(sigmasq);
}
model {
  beta0         ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_age      ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_bmi      ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_children ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_sex      ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_smoker   ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_se       ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_sw       ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_nw       ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  sigmasq       ~ inv_gamma(.01, .01);
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n = beta0
      + beta_age      * age[n]
      + beta_bmi      * bmi[n]
      + beta_children * children[n]
      + beta_sex      * sex[n]
      + beta_smoker   * smoker[n]
      + beta_se       * region_SE[n]
      + beta_sw       * region_SW[n]
      + beta_nw       * region_NW[n];
    y[n] ~ lognormal(mu_n, sigma);
  }
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] yrep;
  real      log_lik[N];
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n   = beta0
      + beta_age      * age[n]
      + beta_bmi      * bmi[n]
      + beta_children * children[n]
      + beta_sex      * sex[n]
      + beta_smoker   * smoker[n]
      + beta_se       * region_SE[n]
      + beta_sw       * region_SW[n]
      + beta_nw       * region_NW[n];
    yrep[n]    = lognormal_rng(mu_n, sigma);
    log_lik[n] = lognormal_lpdf(y[n] | mu_n, sigma);
  }
}
"
model3_data = list(
  N         = N,
  y         = y,
  age       = insurance_data$age,
  bmi       = insurance_data$bmi,
  children  = insurance_data$children,
  sex       = insurance_data$sex_male,
  smoker    = insurance_data$smoker_yes,
  region_SE = as.integer(insurance_data$region=="southeast"),
  region_SW = as.integer(insurance_data$region=="southwest"),
  region_NW = as.integer(insurance_data$region=="northwest")
)

if (!file.exists("model3_mod.rda")) {
  model3_mod <- stan_model(model_code = model3_code)
  save(model3_mod, file = "model3_mod.rda", compress = "xz")
} else {
  load("model3_mod.rda")
}

fit3 <- sampling(model3_mod,
                 data = model3_data,
                 iter=10000, warmup=5000, seed = 101, chains = 4, refresh = 0)

Convergence check

stan_dens(fit3,
          pars = c("beta0",
                   "beta_age", "beta_bmi",
                   "beta_children", "beta_sex", "beta_smoker",
                   "beta_se", "beta_sw", "beta_nw",
                   "sigmasq"),
          separate_chains = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Model 3: Posterior Densities for All β’s and σ²")

Model 4: + Smoker × Age Interaction

Linear predictor
\[ \begin{aligned} \eta_i = \beta_0 &+ \beta_{\text{age}}\,\text{age}_i + \beta_{\text{bmi}}\,\text{bmi}_i + \beta_{\text{children}}\,\text{children}_i \\ &+ \beta_{\text{sex}}\,\text{sex}_i + \beta_{\text{smoker}}\,\text{smoker}_i + \beta_{\text{smoke×age}}\,(\text{smoker}_i \times \text{age}_i) \\ &+ \beta_{\text{SE}}\,\text{region_SE}_i + \beta_{\text{SW}}\,\text{region_SW}_i + \beta_{\text{NW}}\,\text{region_NW}_i \end{aligned} \]

Data model
\[ y_i \sim \operatorname{LogNormal}(\eta_i,\;\sigma^2) \]

Priors
\[ \beta_j \;\sim\; \mathcal{N}(0,\;100^2) \quad\forall j,\qquad \sigma^2 \;\sim\; \operatorname{InvGamma}(0.01,\,0.01) \]

model4_code = "
data {
  int<lower=1>       N;
  vector<lower=0>[N] y;
  vector[N]          age;
  vector[N]          bmi;
  int<lower=0>       children[N];
  vector[N]          sex;
  vector[N]          smoker;
  vector[N]          smoke_age;
  vector[N]          region_SE;
  vector[N]          region_SW;
  vector[N]          region_NW;
}
parameters {
  real beta0;
  real beta_age;
  real beta_bmi;
  real beta_children;
  real beta_sex;
  real beta_smoker;
  real beta_smoke_age;
  real beta_se;
  real beta_sw;
  real beta_nw;
  real<lower=0> sigmasq;
}
transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma = sqrt(sigmasq);
}
model {
  beta0          ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_age       ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_bmi       ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_children  ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_sex       ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_smoker    ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_smoke_age ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_se        ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_sw        ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_nw        ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  sigmasq        ~ inv_gamma(0.01, 0.01);
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n = beta0
      + beta_age       * age[n]
      + beta_bmi       * bmi[n]
      + beta_children  * children[n]
      + beta_sex       * sex[n]
      + beta_smoker    * smoker[n]
      + beta_smoke_age * smoke_age[n]
      + beta_se        * region_SE[n]
      + beta_sw        * region_SW[n]
      + beta_nw        * region_NW[n];
    y[n] ~ lognormal(mu_n, sigma);
  }
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] yrep;
  real      log_lik[N];
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n     = beta0
      + beta_age       * age[n]
      + beta_bmi       * bmi[n]
      + beta_children  * children[n]
      + beta_sex       * sex[n]
      + beta_smoker    * smoker[n]
      + beta_smoke_age * smoke_age[n]
      + beta_se        * region_SE[n]
      + beta_sw        * region_SW[n]
      + beta_nw        * region_NW[n];
    yrep[n]      = lognormal_rng(mu_n, sigma);
    log_lik[n]   = lognormal_lpdf(y[n] | mu_n, sigma);
  }
}
"
model4_data = c(
  model3_data,
  list(smoke_age = insurance_data$age * insurance_data$smoker_yes)
)

if (!file.exists("model4_mod.rda")) {
  model4_mod <- stan_model(model_code = model4_code)
  save(model4_mod, file = "model4_mod.rda", compress = "xz")
} else {
  load("model4_mod.rda")
}

fit4 <- sampling(model4_mod,
                 data = model4_data, 
                 iter=10000, warmup=5000, seed = 101, chains = 4, refresh = 0)

Convergence check

stan_dens(fit4,
          pars = c("beta0",
                   "beta_age", "beta_bmi",
                   "beta_children", "beta_sex", "beta_smoker",
                   "beta_smoke_age",
                   "beta_se", "beta_sw", "beta_nw",
                   "sigmasq"),
          separate_chains = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Model 4: Posterior Densities (including Smoker×Age)")

Model 5: Varying Intercepts by Region

Let \(r_i\) be the region index of observation \(i\), with \(r_i\in\{1,\dots,R\}\). Introduce a separate intercept for each region.

Hierarchical predictor
\[ \eta_i = \beta_0 + a_{r_i} + \beta_{\text{age}}\,\text{age}_i + \beta_{\text{bmi}}\,\text{bmi}_i + \beta_{\text{children}}\,\text{children}_i + \beta_{\text{sex}}\,\text{sex}_i + \beta_{\text{smoker}}\,\text{smoker}_i \]

Data model
\[ y_i \sim \operatorname{LogNormal}(\eta_i,\;\sigma^2) \]

Priors
\[ \begin{aligned} \beta_j &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,\;100^2)\quad\forall j,\\ a_r &\sim \mathcal{N}(0,\;\tau^2)\quad r=1,\dots,R,\\ \tau^2 &\sim \operatorname{InvGamma}(0.01,\,0.01),\\ \sigma^2 &\sim \operatorname{InvGamma}(0.01,\,0.01). \end{aligned} \]

model5_code = "
data {
  int<lower=1>       N;
  int<lower=1>       R;
  int<lower=1,upper=R> region_id[N];
  vector<lower=0>[N] y;
  vector[N]          age;
  vector[N]          bmi;
  int<lower=0>       children[N];
  vector[N]          sex;
  vector[N]          smoker;
}
parameters {
  real              beta0;
  vector[R]         a_region;
  real<lower=0>     sigmasq_region;
  real              beta_age;
  real              beta_bmi;
  real              beta_children;
  real              beta_sex;
  real              beta_smoker;
  real<lower=0>     sigmasq;
}
transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma = sqrt(sigmasq);
  real<lower=0> sigma_region = sqrt(sigmasq_region);
}
model {
  beta0         ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_age      ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_bmi      ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_children ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_sex      ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  beta_smoker   ~ normal(0, 100^2);
  a_region      ~ normal(0, sigma_region);
  sigmasq_region ~ inv_gamma(0.01, 0.01);
  sigmasq       ~ inv_gamma(0.01, 0.01);
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n = beta0
      + a_region[region_id[n]]
      + beta_age      * age[n]
      + beta_bmi      * bmi[n]
      + beta_children * children[n]
      + beta_sex      * sex[n]
      + beta_smoker   * smoker[n];
    y[n] ~ lognormal(mu_n, sigma);
  }
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] yrep;
  real      log_lik[N];
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n    = beta0
      + a_region[region_id[n]]
      + beta_age      * age[n]
      + beta_bmi      * bmi[n]
      + beta_children * children[n]
      + beta_sex      * sex[n]
      + beta_smoker   * smoker[n];
    yrep[n]     = lognormal_rng(mu_n, sigma);
    log_lik[n]  = lognormal_lpdf(y[n] | mu_n, sigma);
  }
}
"
model5_data = list(
  N         = N,
  R         = length(unique(insurance_data$region_id)),
  region_id = insurance_data$region_id,
  y         = y,
  age       = insurance_data$age,
  bmi       = insurance_data$bmi,
  children  = insurance_data$children,
  sex       = insurance_data$sex_male,
  smoker    = insurance_data$smoker_yes
)

if (!file.exists("model5_mod.rda")) {
  model5_mod <- stan_model(model_code = model5_code)
  save(model5_mod, file = "model5_mod.rda", compress = "xz")
} else {
  load("model5_mod.rda")
}

load("model5_mod.rda")
fit5 <- sampling(model5_mod,
                 data = model5_data,
                 iter=10000, warmup=5000, seed = 101, chains = 4, refresh = 0)

Convergence check

stan_dens(fit5,
          pars = c("beta0",
                   "a_region[1]", "a_region[2]", "a_region[3]", "a_region[4]",
                   "beta_age", "beta_bmi", "beta_children",
                   "beta_sex", "beta_smoker",
                   "sigma_region", "sigmasq"),
          separate_chains = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Model 5: Posterior Densities for Varying Intercepts & Fixed Effects")

Selecting best model

# Model 1
log_lik1 <- extract_log_lik(fit1, parameter_name = "log_lik")
waic1    <- waic(log_lik1)
loo1     <- loo(log_lik1)

# Model 2
log_lik2 <- extract_log_lik(fit2, parameter_name = "log_lik")
waic2    <- waic(log_lik2)
loo2     <- loo(log_lik2)

# Model 3
log_lik3 <- extract_log_lik(fit3, parameter_name = "log_lik")
waic3    <- waic(log_lik3)
loo3     <- loo(log_lik3)

# Model 4
log_lik4 <- extract_log_lik(fit4, parameter_name = "log_lik")
waic4    <- waic(log_lik4)
Warning: 
5 (0.4%) p_waic estimates greater than 0.4. We recommend trying loo instead.
loo4     <- loo(log_lik4)

# Model 5
log_lik5 <- extract_log_lik(fit5, parameter_name = "log_lik")
waic5    <- waic(log_lik5)
loo5     <- loo(log_lik5)
# Put your waic & loo objects into lists
waic_list <- list(
  Model1 = waic1,
  Model2 = waic2,
  Model3 = waic3,
  Model4 = waic4,
  Model5 = waic5
)

loo_list <- list(
  Model1 = loo1,
  Model2 = loo2,
  Model3 = loo3,
  Model4 = loo4,
  Model5 = loo5
)


comparison_df <- data.frame(
  Model = names(waic_list),
  WAIC  = sapply(waic_list, function(w) w$estimates["waic","Estimate"]),
  LOOIC = sapply(loo_list,  function(l) l$estimates["looic","Estimate"])
)

Interpretation

  • Starting point \(\beta_{0} \approx 6.801\ [6.668,\ 6.937]\);
    On the log scale, the baseline prediction is 6.801 for someone age 0, BMI 0, no children, female non‐smoker in the Northeast. Exponentiating gives \(\exp(6.801)\approx\$901\), which is the charge we’d predict before adding any other effects.

  • Age \(\beta_{age} \approx 0.041\ [0.039,\ 0.043]\);
    Comparing two people who are identical in BMI, number of children, sex, smoking status, and region, the one who is one year older has a charge about \(\exp(0.041)\approx1.042\) times as large. That is, 4.2% higher.

  • BMI \(\beta_{bmi} \approx 0.012\ [0.009,\ 0.016]\);
    Comparing two people of the same age, children, sex, smoking status, and region, the one with a BMI higher by one point has a charge about \(\exp(0.012)\approx1.012\) times as large. That is, 1.2% higher.

  • Number of children \(\beta_{children} \approx 0.105\ [0.087,\ 0.123]\);
    Comparing two people who match in age, BMI, sex, smoking status, and region, the one with one additional child has a charge about \(\exp(0.105)\approx1.111\) times as large. That is, 11.1% higher.

  • Sex (male vs female) \(\beta_{sex} \approx -0.073\ [-0.117,\ -0.029]\);
    Comparing a male and a female with the same age, BMI, children, smoking status, and region, the male’s predicted charge is about \(\exp(-0.073)\approx0.93\) times the female’s. That is, 7.0% lower.

  • Smoking (yes vs no) \(\beta_{smoker} \approx 2.780\ [2.621,\ 2.941]\);
    Comparing a smoker and a non-smoker of the same age, BMI, children, sex, and region, the smoker’s charge is about \(\exp(2.780)\approx16.1\) times as large. That is, a 1510% increase.

  • Smoking×Age interaction \(\beta_{smoke\times age} \approx -0.032\ [-0.036,\ -0.028]\);
    Among smokers who match in BMI, children, sex, and region, the one who is one year older has a charge about \(\exp(0.041 - 0.032)\approx\exp(0.009)\approx1.009\) times as large. That is, 0.9% higher per year of age for smokers.

  • Region: Southeast vs Northeast \(\beta_{SE} \approx -0.139\ [-0.203,\ -0.077]\);
    Comparing two people of the same age, BMI, children, sex, and smoking status, the one living in the Southeast has a charge about \(\exp(-0.139)\approx0.87\) times as large. That is, 13.0% lower.

  • Region: Southwest vs Northeast \(\beta_{SW} \approx -0.140\ [-0.204,\ -0.077]\);
    Under the same comparison, a Southwest resident’s charge is \(\exp(-0.140)\approx0.87\) times as large. That is, 13.1% lower.

  • Region: Northwest vs Northeast \(\beta_{NW} \approx -0.057\ [-0.120,\ 0.006]\);
    Under the same comparison, a Northwest resident’s charge is \(\exp(-0.057)\approx0.945\) times as large. That is, 5.5% lower, but the credible interval of the parameter includes 0, so this effect is uncertain.
